question.text: The Subscription Agreement for Tungabhadra Infrastructure Fund requires investors to make representations about their 'eligible investor' status. Under SEBI AIF Regulations, what is the general minimum capital commitment from an investor to an AIF?

answer.text: INR 1 crore (subject to exceptions for employees/directors, accredited investors, and angel-fund investments by angel investors)

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI AIF Regulations set a general minimum capital commitment of INR 1 crore per investor. The workbook also recognises specific exceptions: employees and directors of the AIF or manager have a lower minimum of INR 25 lakh, and separate frameworks apply to accredited investors and to angel-fund investments by angel investors. The INR 1 crore figure is the general rule rather than an absolute cap that applies to every AIF investor in every situation. The Trap: INR 25 lakh is the concessional limit for employees/directors and is often confused with the general investor minimum; INR 5 crore and INR 10 crore are distractors with no regulatory basis as the standard floor. Note: Kept the INR 1 crore general-rule answer but removed the absolute 'any AIF' wording and added the accredited-investor and angel-fund exceptions alongside the employee/director exception.
